skill.name: limrun-ios-simulator
skill.description: Control apps on Limrun cloud iOS simulators through the lim CLI. Launch apps, inspect accessibility, interact with screens, capture media, manage files, and test camera flows.
skill.summary: Automate iOS app testing and media capture on Limrun cloud simulators.
skill.author: limrun-inc

security_audit.summary: All 113 static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown, documented CLI operations, normal temporary output, and benign credential references. The skill still requires safeguards for global package installation, cloud artifact uploads, and signed simulator links.

remediation.issue: The installation command uses an unpinned global npm package.
remediation.suggestion: Pin an audited lim version and request approval before installation. Prefer a project-scoped package or verified package runner when supported.

remediation.issue: Local app bundles and assets are uploaded to Limrun.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit consent before every upload. State the destination and selected path, then check artifacts for secrets and production data.

remediation.issue: Signed simulator links provide session access.
remediation.suggestion: Treat signed URLs as credentials. Share them only with the requesting user, avoid logs, and document expiration or revocation.

content.user_title: Test iOS Apps in a Cloud Simulator
content.value_statement: iOS UI testing often requires macOS hardware and manual simulator access. This skill controls Limrun cloud simulators through the lim CLI from any supported environment.
actual_capabilities: Creates or selects a Limrun cloud iOS simulator.
Launches, terminates, and relaunches installed apps by bundle identifier.
Reads accessibility elements and performs taps, typing, scrolling, swipes, and timed actions.
Captures screenshots and simulator video recordings.
Lists, uploads, downloads, and deletes files in an app container.
Feeds a local video into the simulated camera for camera-driven tests.
limitations: Requires the lim CLI, Limrun authentication, and an available cloud simulator.
Does not build iOS applications or replace the separate Limrun build skills.
Some SwiftUI toolbar controls require coordinate taps because accessibility identifiers may be unavailable.
Automated text injection may not trigger every SwiftUI or React Native state update.

use_cases.title: Validate a feature change
use_cases.description: Launch the updated app, exercise the changed flow, and verify visible state through accessibility output and screenshots.

use_cases.title: Run remote acceptance checks
use_cases.description: Follow a repeatable action sequence, capture evidence, and report where observed behavior differs from acceptance criteria.

use_cases.title: Review an app without macOS
use_cases.description: Open a signed browser stream, inspect the current build, and review recorded interactions from a supported environment.

prompt_templates.title: Launch and inspect an app
prompt_templates.prompt: Launch [bundle ID] in the Limrun iOS simulator. Read the accessibility tree, take a screenshot, and summarize the visible screen.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner inspection of an installed application.

prompt_templates.title: Verify one interaction
prompt_templates.prompt: Open [bundle ID], locate [control label or accessibility ID], activate it, and confirm [expected result] through the element tree.
prompt_templates.scenario: Focused validation of one user interface change.

prompt_templates.title: Record a complete flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Run [steps] on simulator [instance ID]. Record the flow, verify each transition, and report failures with the relevant interface state.
prompt_templates.scenario: Repeatable acceptance testing with visual evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Test a camera workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Install [app bundle], play [video path] as the simulator camera, execute [action file], and validate [expected outcomes]. Preserve diagnostic screenshots and recordings.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced automated testing of camera-dependent behavior.

output_examples.input: Launch com.example.app and confirm that the welcome screen appears.
output: The app launched successfully on the selected simulator.
The accessibility tree contains the Welcome heading and Continue button.
A screenshot was captured for visual review.

output_examples.input: Tap Save, verify the confirmation message, and record the interaction.
output: The Save control was activated through its accessibility identifier.
The confirmation message appeared after the action.
The recording contains the complete interaction and final state.

output_examples.input: Use the QR fixture as the camera and verify the scan result.
output: The fixture video was supplied to the simulated camera.
The app displayed the expected scan result.
The camera feed was cleared after validation.

best_practices: Confirm the target simulator and bundle identifier before changing app state.
Prefer accessibility identifiers, then labels, and use coordinates only when necessary.
Request consent before uploads and protect signed simulator links as credentials.
anti_patterns: Do not guess unsupported flags when command help can confirm the syntax.
Do not upload app bundles, fixtures, or container files without user approval.
Do not rely on screenshots alone for functional assertions or dynamic state.

faq.question: Does this skill build the iOS application?
faq.answer: No. Build the app with a compatible Limrun build skill, then use this skill for simulator interaction and testing.

faq.question: Can it run without macOS or local Xcode?
faq.answer: Yes. The simulator runs in Limrun cloud infrastructure and the lim CLI can operate from supported environments.

faq.question: How does the skill select a simulator?
faq.answer: It can use the recent workspace instance or an explicit instance identifier. Explicit identifiers are recommended when multiple simulators exist.

faq.question: Can it capture screenshots and video?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports screenshots, nonblocking recording, and saved recording files for review.

faq.question: Can it test camera-based features?
faq.answer: Yes. It can play an AVFoundation-compatible video as the simulator camera and restore the default feed afterward.

faq.question: What data can leave the local environment?
faq.answer: App bundles, media fixtures, and selected assets may be uploaded to Limrun. Review the files and obtain user consent first.
